waivers.reason: Headings, an explanatory note, and a lead-in whose concrete pure-function prohibitions occur in subsequent list anchors have no standalone claim.
Warning text, headings, simulator-defined out-of-DPI behavior, and explanatory call-chain definitions/examples do not add a portable independently testable outcome.
List framing, explicitly undefined control-transfer behavior, and implementation-defined enablement/user handle management provide no separate portable conformance oracle.
Optimization-barrier characterization is not independently observable when externally visible language semantics are preserved.
Heading, motivation, list lead-in, and restatement of immediately preceding mandatory items add no independent behavior.

Protocol overview repeats detailed rules, while values returned or written during disabled imported-subroutine return are explicitly undefined and need not be propagated, providing no portable value oracle.

This is a user foreign-code memory-ownership obligation, but violation has no standard-prescribed portable result; allocator corruption, crashes, and external allocator instrumentation are not trustworthy language conformance oracles.
Syntax caption and heading add no independent behavior.
Heading only; the permitted-type rules are cataloged from the following normative blocks.
Cross-reference, heading, syntax caption, and informative note add no behavior beyond associated normative blocks.
Cross-reference, example lead-in and code, and heading add no independent behavior.
Headings, broad equivalence descriptions, interface roadmap, and explicitly implementation-dependent representation text provide context but no additional portable independently scored behavior.
Headings, examples, user/tool guidance, and broad introductory similarity statements add no independent normative behavior.
Example lead-ins and code plus headings add no independent normative behavior.
The initial value of an imported output formal is explicitly unspecified and potentially implementation dependent, so it has no portable value oracle.
Topic-list entries, headings, motivation, architectural overview, and black-box rationale provide context but no independently falsifiable language rule beyond detailed provisions elsewhere.

Pure-function side-effect and input-determinism restrictions are user foreign-code promises. Violations have optimizer-dependent unexpected behavior, while conforming implementations need not eliminate or cache calls, so there is no portable required runtime result.
Clause and subclause headings plus the introductory topic list only identify the DPI subject matter; they state no independently testable language behavior.
Headings, roadmap text, notes, and explicitly undetermined implementation-dependent initial output values have no additional portable oracle; detailed rules are cataloged separately.
List lead-in, implementation-dependent representation statement, and heading have no separate portable behavior.
Headings, user responsibility for cross-language matching, and an illustrative restatement add no independent portable behavior.
